non_blocking: No ABANDON. None of the five named candidates contains claim (a) (NONE-option judge choosing wrong candidates from all-wrong pools, more than isolated verification, moderated by solvability) or claim (b) (forced pick = the wrong candidate the same model's verification passes most). The checks below were run against the actual papers, not only search snippets.

arXiv 2402.01349 (Wang et al., COLING 2025, the same paper as wang2025llms): section 4.2 'MCQA with No Correct Option' prompts models with 'no answer' over all-wrong MCQs and finds ChatGPT-4o picks it in about 60% of cases. Section 3.5 hypothesises that LLMs 'treat the selected option as the most accurate among the choices'. This is adjacent to (a) and (b) but has no isolated-verification arm, no same-model verify-after-select test and no solvability moderation. Cite it as related work and drop any suggestion that it anticipates the result.

arXiv 2503.01550 'None of the Above, Less of the Right' (Mar 2025): NA as the correct answer in MMLU causes a 30-50% drop across 28 LLMs. This is the reverse failure (not picking NONE when it is right), so it does not show a NONE option choosing wrong candidates. Cite it as related NONE-option work. Cite it in the paper; it is the closest published NONE-option result.

arXiv 2510.04087 (Best of mini-N in-loop): a reward model trained with an outside option to avoid 'the least bad of many unacceptable options'. It trains a reward model on IMDB sentiment and does not test LLM judges on target-absent pools. Related work on outside options, not overlapping.

arXiv 2611.00507 'Selecting or Solving?' (accepted NeurIPS 2026 VLM4WRD workshop): best-of-N video selection, with Selection Increment as the verifier's gain over its own accuracy with candidates withheld. Not NONE-option, not all-wrong pools, not isolated-versus-pooled. Related only in the 'selecting versus solving' framing, which the paper could cite as an adjacent decomposition.

NeurIPS 2026 poster 'Selected-Tail Reliability in Verifier-Guided Best-of-N Inference' (https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/poster/155878, Teresa Zhang, posted 2026-09-25): studies selected-rank exposure laws and tail certification for verifier-guided BoN. It has no LLM-judge NONE option and no lineup-style comparison. Only the search summary of the abstract was readable; the full text was not. Not overlapping, but a related selection-reliability work the paper should cite.

arXiv 2608.25937 (ji2026candidate): states 'No selection rule can recover a correct answer when no correct candidate' and excludes all-wrong pools. This is the paper's stated gap, and the manuscript already cites it correctly.

Recommendation: add 2402.01349 section 4.2 and 2503.01550 to related work. The manuscript's Related work does not mention either, so a reviewer could raise the NONE-option literature as an omission (non-blocking).
